info.title: Hospital Asset Management System (HAMS) API
info.description: Microservices architecture for tracking and transferring hospital assets between wards. Each service exposes its own GraphQL endpoint and owns a dedicated MySQL database — there is no shared database between services (database-per-service pattern). The API Gateway proxies GraphQL requests to the correct service based on URL path; it does not touch any database itself. Cross-service communication (e.g. asset-service logging a notification, transfer-service validating an asset) happens by calling the owning service's GraphQL endpoint, never by reaching into another service's database directly.

servers.description: API Gateway — routes /graphql/{service} to the corresponding microservice

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: auth-service — owns auth_db (users table). Handles registration, login, JWT issuance and verification.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description: asset-service — owns asset_db (assets, maintenance_reports, maintenance_actions tables). Handles asset inventory, QR codes, and maintenance/damage reports.

tags.name: Wards
tags.description: ward-service — owns ward_db (wards table). Handles the list of hospital wards/locations.

tags.name: Transfers
tags.description: transfer-service — owns transfer_db (transfers, notifikasi tables). Handles inter-ward asset transfers and is the single source of truth for notifications; other services call its addNotification mutation rather than writing notifications directly.

post.description:
Available operations:

Queries:
- verifyToken — validates the JWT in the Authorization header
- users — list all users (admin only)

Mutations:
- register(username, password, role) — create a user account
- login(username, password) — returns a JWT token
- deleteUser(id) — admin only, cannot delete own account

example.query: mutation Login($u: String!, $p: String!) { login(username: $u, password: $p) { message token user { id username role } } }

200.description: GraphQL response (200 is returned even for resolver-level errors; check the `errors` field)

post.summary: Asset Service GraphQL endpoint (also handles maintenance reports/actions)
post.description:
Available operations:

Queries:
- assets — full asset inventory
- assetByQR(hash) — look up one asset by QR hash
- maintenanceReports — all maintenance reports, newest first
- maintenanceByAsset(asset_id) — maintenance history for one asset
- generateQR(hash) — base64 QR code image

Mutations:
- addAsset(name, type, sub_category, current_ward, qr_hash)
- updateAssetLocation(id, current_ward, status)
- updateWardName(id, ward_name) — cascades the new name to all assets currently in that ward
- deleteAsset(id) — blocked if status is In Use or In Transit
- createMaintenanceReport(asset_id, asset_name, type, report_date, description, reporter) — also calls transfer-service's addNotification
- addMaintenanceAction(report_id, start_date, estimated_end_date, action_date, vendor, cost, duration_days, notes, status) — also calls transfer-service's addNotification

example.query: mutation AddAsset($name: String!, $ward: String!, $hash: String!) { addAsset(name: $name, current_ward: $ward, qr_hash: $hash) { message } }

200.description: GraphQL response (200 is returned even for resolver-level errors; check the `errors` field)

post.description:
Available operations:

Queries:
- wards — full ward list

Mutations:
- addWard(ward_name) — fails with a clear error if the ward already exists
- deleteWard(id)

200.description: GraphQL response (200 is returned even for resolver-level errors; check the `errors` field)

post.description:
Available operations:

Queries:
- activeTransfer(asset_id) — the in-progress transfer for an asset, if any
- transferHistory — full transfer log, newest first
- notifikasiList — all logged notifications, newest first (used by the frontend bell icon)

Mutations:
- initiateTransfer(qr_hash, from_ward, to_ward) — validates the asset via asset-service's GraphQL endpoint before logging the transfer
- receiveTransfer(id) — marks a transfer Completed and updates the asset's location via asset-service
- cancelTransfer(asset_id) — reverts an In Transit transfer
- addNotification(tier, teks) — single write path for the notifikasi table; called by other services instead of them writing to it directly

example.query: mutation Initiate($hash: String!, $from: String!, $to: String!) { initiateTransfer(qr_hash: $hash, from_ward: $from, to_ward: $to) { message transfer_id } }

200.description: GraphQL response (200 is returned even for resolver-level errors; check the `errors` field). A 400-style failure (e.g. asset not available) surfaces in `errors[0].message`.
